subject.title: fix: deliver Codex-generated images on message-tool routes

question: Should `message_tool_only` permit explicitly provider-classified host-owned terminal artifacts across all harnesses, or should this exception remain Codex-specific until a shared contract is designed?
rationale: The implementation is technically focused, but it changes the permanent meaning of a shared delivery policy and exports an authorization-like signal through the common harness result type; code review cannot safely choose that product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Approve a generic host-owned contract
options.body: Define which harness-owned terminal outputs may bypass source suppression, document their invariants, and add focused sibling-harness coverage before merge.

options.title: Constrain the exception to Codex
options.body: Keep the delivery exception within the Codex-owned integration path and avoid exposing a general bypass signal until other harnesses have a concrete need.

options.title: Pause for broader policy design
options.body: Defer this PR if maintainers want `message_tool_only` to remain an absolute suppression policy for all provider artifacts.

recommendation.title: Approve a generic host-owned contract
recommendation.body: Define which harness-owned terminal outputs may bypass source suppression, document their invariants, and add focused sibling-harness coverage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline assigns steipete to this protected maintainer-labeled PR, and the remaining blocker is an owner-level contract decision.
